speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To begin our evaluation, have you or your family ever received a diagnosis of osteogenesis imperfecta or brittle bone disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient reports severe acne, partial labial fusion, clitoromegaly, and a history of fractures with minor trauma, but denies a prior diagnosis of osteogenesis imperfecta. Given the combination of bone fragility, ambiguous genitalia, and early signs of virilization (acne, hirsutism), do you have any family history of similar symptoms, and have any blood tests been done to check for androgen levels or bone density?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency).

The clinical picture of ambiguous genitalia at birth, virilization (acne, hirsutism), and bone fragility strongly suggests 21-hydroxylase deficiency, which can lead to adrenal insufficiency and delayed puberty. I need to confirm this by checking your steroid hormone levels.

REQUEST TEST: Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone, Androgens, and ACTH stimulation test.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound_to_assess_uterus_and_ovaries.
